🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-21 23:00 → 2026-10-22 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **ERC-8004 conformance harness completed full mutation kill coverage** — property-based testing eliminated all 22 mutations, delivering a definitive quality benchmark for the spec's test suite. [PR #12](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/12)

> **Spec drift detection tooling opened as ERC-8004 research** — new work traces obligation coverage against live spec text, enabling early detection when tests and the spec begin to diverge. [PR #13](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/13)

> **Recompute-kit evidence-only probe verified green at a specific commit** — independent review confirmed the probe exits with code 2 and the main suite holds 32/32, giving the team a clean verification anchor. [PR #83 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/83#issuecomment-6344533492)

> **ERC-8004 review methodology validated in open discussion** — isolating follow-up changes as a Draft PR with frozen prior heads was confirmed as the right approach for preserving a replayable review baseline. [tg:tawg:5672]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### ERC-8004 conformance
_The conformance harness advanced from registry foundations through reviewer-driven gap isolation, with the full group engaged in validating the review structure._

- Pavlo **Opened** a registry pilot PR for the reusable ERC-8004 conformance harness, creating the structural foundation for shared test infrastructure across the group's tooling. [PR #10](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/10)

- Pavlo **Isolated** four reviewer-identified coverage gaps in a focused follow-up PR, keeping the feedback loop tight and the gap surface explicitly bounded for the next review pass. [PR #11](https://github.com/trustless-ai/verifiable-execution-claim-authorization/pull/11)

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Shared** a morning update crediting Echo and Panini's independent replay of #9 and explaining the follow-up plan, keeping the full group oriented on how reviewer feedback shaped the next steps. [tg:tawg:5670]

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Observed** that the scenario matrix and mutation coverage together form a strong review foundation, helping the group calibrate confidence before moving deeper into spec work. [tg:tawg:5677]

### recompute-kit
_A long-standing correctness issue closed while cross-repo experience sharing and independent verification added depth to the team's review confidence._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Shipped** the fix that makes the conformance suite refuse a manifest it cannot read rather than marking it refuted, closing issue #72 and removing a misleading conformance result from the toolchain. [PR #80](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/80)

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Shared** structural patterns from prior execution-specs work that map directly onto recompute-kit's organization, bridging external experience into the group's active tooling decisions. [tg:tawg:5680]

- Echo **Acknowledged** on the PR thread that Zexo's earlier identification of the correctness issue should have been acted on sooner, modeling healthy shared ownership of the toolchain's quality decisions. [PR #80 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/80#issuecomment-6351908959)

- Baby Blue Viper **Described** a production anchor-check approach using a daily Merkle snapshot of receipt slots, offering a concrete real-world reference for the group's ongoing anchor-check design work. [tg:tawg:5693]

### ERC-8183
_The agentic commerce thread received a new edge-case contribution on deterministic evaluator behavior._

- A contributor **Added** a case from running a live deterministic evaluator showing that triggering payment on silence produces a worse outcome, surfacing an underspecified edge in obligation design that the thread has not yet resolved. [ERC-8183 thread](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/431)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- The spec drift detection approach could open a broader group conversation about tracking spec-test divergence across all active ERC efforts, not only ERC-8004.
- Baby Blue Viper's production Merkle snapshot recipe may serve as a direct reference pattern for the anchor-check design work already underway.
- The ERC-8183 payment-on-silence edge case may benefit from a focused reply that works through how obligation triggers should handle evaluator silence.

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Review ERC-8004 PRs #10, #11, #12, and #13 to give Pavlo feedback across the registry, gap isolation, mutation coverage, and spec drift work.
- Complete review of recompute-kit PR #80 now that the fix is in and independent verification is on record.
- Follow up on the execution-specs pattern mapping Zexo outlined to identify the most transferable improvements for recompute-kit organization.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** Morning reviewer feedback turned into a coverage-gap PR before noon, which was followed by two research PRs on mutation coverage and spec drift before the window closed — one review cycle feeding three forward moves.
>
> When the feedback loop runs this clean, the whole codebase keeps up. Stay in the loop 🔄
